description:
Add one component of ANY registered type — a collider, a rigid body, a joint, a light, a material, a geometry … — to a saved R3 project, with its values and references set before it is created. Kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now, no editor needed and nothing to save (r3_editor_add_component is the same tool). Use r3_factory_run for a ready-made object (a cube, a physics sphere …).

`type` is the short type name, e.g. "ColliderCuboid" (an unknown type is refused with the list). `values` take r3_component_set's shapes: a plain value {"friction": 0.2}; a value component as the keys to set {"halfExtents": {"x": 2, "y": 0.5, "z": 1}}; a reference as the target's entityRef or id {"rigidBody": "rigidbody_dynamic_1"} — a component of THIS project, of a type the slot accepts; "name" names it. A type that cannot exist without an option (an Audio / AudioPositional / Texture's "url") takes it in values too, and is refused without it. A Code component's code is r3_code_write's. A VehicleWheel added with a mesh is measured from it (Configure from Mesh: radius, connectionPoint, axle), and a ColliderCuboid / Sphere / Cylinder / Capsule with a mesh (its own or its rigid body's) is fitted to it (Fit to Mesh: size, and position on the mesh's centre), only the values you did not pass; the answer says what (PHYSICS_USAGE.md → Vehicles).
name: r3_component_add

answer.description: This answer in words: what was done, what R3 measured, decided or refused, and what to do next. The same text as the result's text block. Read it: the fields beside it are the data, this is the guidance.

title: Add ANY component to a saved R3 project
